metadata.title: The Mask Slips.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Annyeong (Korean), one word — fresh for this channel (Namaste, Kumusta, Sawubona, Hej, Merhaba, Jambo and Vanakkam are spent on the seven prior reels). IN-FOR-BEAR LAW in its Yatra form: Bella is the STAND-IN VOICE on Yatra's own @Yatra channel, so the greeting slot carries the NARRATOR's name, B00's first breath says the voice out loud, and the outro signs off the same way. Footer chip stays @Yatra. Voice: Kokoro af_bella (free, local).
metadata.color_semantics: Fidelity claude palette. ONE terracotta #D97757 event per beat, and it always marks THE COLLAPSE SIDE of the story — the fall after the spike, the moment of identification, the engagement that went away. The rise is rendered in plain ink: the accent is reserved for what the reel is actually warning about, so the gold-rush half is never the thing that glows. Source lines stay muted ink, never accent.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, ask lands ANSWERED), B04 (ask micro-beat of the one ask→result pair, resolved by B05), B10 (verdict artifact), B11 (handoff), B12 (outro). Every other beat illustrates with a purpose-built Msk* scene. SOURCING (hard, per the human): every figure in this reel comes from ONE report — Garbage Day, October 2026 — and every scene that renders a figure REQUIRES a `source` string, so a number cannot reach the screen uncited. NO INVENTED NUMBERS AND NO INVENTED DETAIL: the supplied figures are 2 days, 26,000 followers, 2.2 million likes, $13,700 from a single video, and a roughly 50% engagement drop on one early account plus the same drop on one other AI persona. Nothing else is numeric anywhere. Neither account is NAMED, because the human did not name them. The money figure keeps its 'reported' hedge on screen and in narration; the engagement drop keeps its 'roughly'.
metadata.derived_from: fresh build — new concept explainer; all eight body scenes are new components (Msk* family), no narration or illustration component reused from any prior reel

beats.narration_text: Hello, this is Bella, in for Yatra. This one is about AI influencers — accounts with nobody behind them — and how fast they can make real money. And how fast that money goes away again.

show.event: Cream page, serif greeting 'Annyeong, Bella' above the composer — the app greets the narrator, the footer chip stays @Yatra
The ask types itself in
Terracotta send arms — the ONE accent
Three result lines stagger in; the third names the collapse — the ask lands ANSWERED

props.command: AI influencer accounts are going viral and earning money within days, then collapsing once audiences work out they are AI. Walk me through the arc — the rise, the reveal, and what happens to engagement after. Cite the reporting on screen and do not add figures that aren't in it.
output: the rise: viral two days after the account was created
the money: a reported $13,700 from one video
the reveal: identified as AI — and roughly half the engagement gone

beats.narration_text: Here's the whole thing in one breath. An AI influencer can go viral in days and earn real money almost immediately. Then people work out there's nobody there — and the audience doesn't drift away, it turns.

show.event: Phase one sets on the left in ink, headed FAST: 'Viral in days. Real money almost immediately.'
A hairline divider draws down the middle as the sentence pivots on 'then'
Phase two sets on the right in TERRACOTTA, headed FASTER: 'People work out there's nobody there.'
The closer lands across the foot: 'A gold rush with a very short shelf life.'

data.slideMeta: The whole arc, before any detail
secondLines: People work out there's nobody there.
data.closer: A gold rush with a very short shelf life.

beats.narration_text: Start with the speed. Garbage Day reported on an AI influencer account that went viral two days after it was created. Two days. Twenty-six thousand followers. Two point two million likes.

show.event: A clock-face figure sets first and holds: TWO DAYS, from account created to viral
Follower figure lands beside it — 26,000 — rendered verbatim, never recomputed
Likes figure lands — 2.2 million
The source line sets in muted ink beneath all three: Garbage Day, October 2026
A single terracotta tick marks the two-day mark on the baseline — the accent is on how little time this took

data.title: Two days from created to viral
data.note: One account. The point is the clock, not the category.

beats.narration_text: And it wasn't only attention. From a single video, that account reportedly made thirteen thousand seven hundred dollars. One video. That's the gold rush part of the story, and it's why everyone is trying it.

show.event: The figure sets very large in ink and holds: $13,700
Its qualifier sets beneath: 'from a single video'
A REPORTED chip sets hard against the figure — the hedge is attached to the number, not hidden in a footnote
Source line in muted ink: Garbage Day, October 2026
The terracotta rule underlines the closing note rather than the figure — the money is not the thing being warned about

data.note: Reported, not audited — and that distinction survives the rest of this video.

beats.narration_text: That's the upside, and it's genuinely fast. I wanted the whole arc drawn — the rise, and what comes after it.

show.event: Composer returns with the generation prompt already arriving
Terracotta send arms
Running indicator reads 'drawing the arc…' — the result is the next beat

props.command: Draw the arc of an AI influencer account: a near-vertical rise to viral, then the fall that starts at the moment the audience identifies it as AI. Mark the identification point. No invented numbers — shape only.

beats.narration_text: And here it is. The rise is almost vertical. But the fall isn't the algorithm getting bored, and it isn't the trend moving on. It starts at one specific moment, and the moment has a name.

show.event: Baseline draws; the curve climbs almost vertically on 'the rise is almost vertical'
The curve crests and holds flat for a beat
A TERRACOTTA marker drops on the crest, labelled 'identified as AI' — the ONE accent, and it is the cause, not the effect
The curve falls away from the marker
The axis is deliberately UNNUMBERED, and a muted line says so: shape only, no figures claimed

data.slideMeta: The shape of the whole thing
data.title: Up fast, down faster
data.axisNote: Shape only — this curve carries no figures.
data.note: The fall has a cause, and the cause is a moment, not a trend.

beats.narration_text: Here's the turn. These accounts work for exactly as long as the audience believes there's a person behind them. The moment people realize there isn't, the relationship they thought they had was never actually there.

show.event: Two nodes draw with a solid wire between them: AUDIENCE and, at the far end, a node labelled 'a person'
The wire is labelled 'the relationship' and sits solid and intact
On 'realize there isn't', the far node is struck through and relabelled — nobody there
The wire does not snap — it turns DASHED along its whole length in TERRACOTTA, retroactively: it was never solid
Closing line sets: 'It didn't break. It was never there.'

data.title: The relationship was the product
data.verdict: It didn't break. It was never there.
data.note: This is why the fall is steeper than ordinary churn.

beats.act: THE DROP — what the numbers did
beats.narration_text: And the numbers move with it. Garbage Day reports that one of the earliest popular AI influencer accounts lost roughly half its engagement after it was identified as AI. And another AI persona has seen the same drop.

show.event: Case one's bar draws to full height in ink, labelled 'before identification'
On 'lost roughly half', the bar visibly halves — the motion enacts the sentence rather than cutting to a second bar
The figure sets beside it, verbatim with its hedge intact: 'roughly 50%'
Case two draws beneath and performs the same halving, labelled 'the same drop'
Both cases are labelled by DESCRIPTION, never by name — neither account is named anywhere in this reel
Source line in muted ink: Garbage Day, October 2026

data.title: Roughly half the engagement, gone

cases.label: one of the earliest popular AI influencer accounts
cases.detail: engagement lost after being identified as AI

data.note: Described, not named — the report's framing is kept as it was given.

beats.narration_text: Notice what that is. It isn't a slow decline, and it isn't people drifting off to something newer. Audiences don't simply lose interest when they find out. They turn. Attention given under a false impression gets taken back.

show.event: Candidate one sets: 'a slow decline' — then rules through as it is dismissed
Candidate two sets: 'people drifting to something newer' — rules through
Candidate three sets: 'the trend moving on' — rules through
The surviving line lands alone and large in TERRACOTTA: 'They turn.'
The closing line sets beneath it: 'Attention given under a false impression gets taken back.'

data.closer: Attention given under a false impression gets taken back.
data.note: The distinction matters: churn you can win back, a turn you cannot.

beats.narration_text: Worth being exact. This is a handful of accounts in one report, not a study of the whole category. The money figure is reported, not audited. And none of it says AI content can't work — only that undisclosed AI content has a cliff built into it.

show.event: Left ledger heads WHAT THE REPORTING SHOWS and three lines stack in
Right ledger heads WHAT IT DOESN'T and its lines stack in TERRACOTTA — the accent sits on the refusals, where the honesty is
A muted provenance rule draws across the foot naming the single source behind every figure in this reel
The falsifier lands last: 'Check the accounts yourself before you believe the pattern.'

data.title: What this is, and isn't

claims.heading: What the reporting shows
items: one account went viral two days after creation
it reportedly earned $13,700 from a single video
two AI accounts lost roughly half their engagement after being identified

refusals.heading: What it doesn't
items: that this is measured across the category — it's a handful of accounts
that the money figure is audited — it is reported
that AI content can't work — only that undisclosed AI content has a cliff

data.provenance: Every figure in this video comes from one report: Garbage Day, October 2026. No other numbers are claimed.
data.falsifier: Check the accounts yourself before you believe the pattern.

beats.narration_text: So — the pattern. Zero to viral in two days. Real money almost immediately. Then identification, and roughly half the engagement gone. A gold rush with a very short shelf life. And if you work in marketing, the lesson isn't avoid AI. It's that authenticity might be the one thing an audience can't be fooled out of caring about.

show.event: Claude artifact page opens
Line one lands — the speed, cited
Line two lands — the money, with its hedge
Line three lands — the drop after identification
Line four lands — the shelf life
Line five lands and holds — the lesson for marketing

artifactLines: The rise: one AI influencer account went viral two days after it was created — 26,000 followers, 2.2 million likes (Garbage Day, October 2026).
The money: a reported $13,700 from a single video. Reported, not audited.
The reveal: one of the earliest popular AI influencer accounts lost roughly 50% of its engagement after being identified as AI. Another AI persona saw the same drop.
The shape: a gold rush with a very short shelf life — the fall begins at identification, not at boredom.
The lesson: this isn't an argument against using AI. It's that authenticity may be the one thing an audience can't be fooled out of caring about.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take something you're about to publish and paste this: tell me which parts of this would lose their meaning if the audience learned a machine made them, and which parts wouldn't care. Look for whether it can tell the difference — because that line is the whole risk.

show.event: Serif 'Your turn.' replaces the persona greeting
The prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim
Terracotta send arms
Three-item rubric stacks in as each check is discussed

props.command: Here's something I'm about to publish. Tell me which parts of it would lose their meaning if my audience learned a machine made them, and which parts wouldn't care either way. Then tell me which of those I'd be embarrassed to have to explain later.
output: grade it: can it tell persuasion from information?
grade it: does it separate 'undisclosed' from 'AI-made'?
grade it: does it name what you'd have to explain later?

beats.narration_text: The mask slips. And it slips fast. This is Bella, in for Yatra — thanks for watching.
